did: I placed home's on-demand deploy in the assurance ledger. It is a new family, Home catches up with the app, with two promises. The first is that home pulls a newer server only when the app asks, and within its bounds. The second is that a deploy that fails or never starts reaches you. I also got the route snapshot with home's new ask through. Then I built the phone's side: when a paired phone starts, comes back to the front, or is pulled down, it asks home whether home works with this version of the app. The sharing marks then say so: home is updating, home can't work with it yet, or the app is older than home.

calls.title: Home's deploy unit runs as root and runs make as you (C83)
options: root, with make run as you
your user throughout, with the deploy folder made group-writable
root throughout, with sops pointed at your key
calls.why: The deploy folder belongs to the server's own user, and the secrets key is yours. Nothing settled a host unit that needs both.
calls.undo: Run the unit as you, keep its runtime folder, and make the deploy folder writable for you.

calls.title: The deploy's ask gets a family and two promises of its own (C84)
options: a family of its own, with new promises
fold it into Home is up as an exception
count it as a request that owes nothing later
calls.why: Home is up spans everything, so no single process may carry it. The deploy's bounds are about wasted work, not uptime. And the ask does owe a later deploy.
calls.undo: Retire the two promises with your decision, and move the ask under Home is up.

left: No clip of the new marks on the phone: I couldn't record the phone's screen from this session.
Three server follow-ups wait in server#782: the alerts still name the uptime promise; an ask home could not write down reaches no one; and nothing tests the deploy's 30-minute stop.
